title: Tresco Group acquires Green Maritime and sets course for seagoing shipping
summary: Antwerp-based Tresco has acquired "Green Maritime," a firm providing operational data from 220 short-sea vessels, claiming to offer precise fuel consumption measurements. This acquisition directly targets the escalating regulatory pressure from EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime, where accurate data is now essential for compliance and avoiding substantial fines. However, merely tracking emissions does not inherently force a reduction in actual carbon intensity or a necessary shift away from excessive high-carbon fuel consumption.
content:
Tresco, the Antwerp-based leader in inland navigation software backed by Strada Partners, has acquired Green Maritime, the Dutch specialist in operational data on board seagoing vessels. Green Maritime’s technology runs on 220 vessels today, mainly in short sea shipping. The deal takes Tresco beyond inland waterways into the much larger seagoing market, where EU climate rules are driving demand for measured fuel and emissions data. It is the next step in Tresco’s ambition to build a broad maritime technology group, through organic growth and targeted acquisitions.

Measured data, straight from on board

Green Maritime collects on-board data on fuel consumption, engine performance and navigation. Shipowners use it to report emissions, cut fuel costs, spot technical problems early and run their fleets more efficiently. The system is affordable and quick to install. Instead of calculating with bunker delivery notes and estimates, it measures what a ship actually burns. Proven in daily operation on 220 vessels, it is ready to scale.

Former sea captain Bart Schut founded Green Maritime in 2020, after seven years at sea and five years running operations at a shipping company. He built the platform around the problems he ran into on board and in the office.

Regulation drives demand

Since 2024, seagoing vessels of 5,000 GT and above fall under the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS). The scheme is being phased in: for emissions from 2026 onwards, shipowners must surrender allowances for 100% of their verified emissions. FuelEU Maritime has applied since 1 January 2025 and lowers the greenhouse gas intensity of the energy used on board step by step. By the end of 2026, the European Commission will assess whether to extend the rules to smaller ships, which could bring short sea vessels and coasters below 5,000 GT into scope.

Both systems rest on accurate measurement. A shipowner who doesn’t know what a ship burns can’t report its emissions correctly, let alone reduce them. The same data keeps fuel costs in check and shows how a fleet performs, so the investment pays off well beyond compliance.

“Regulation is driving innovation in the maritime sector,” said Evert Bulcke, CEO of Tresco Group. “The rules are mostly European, but their impact reaches far beyond Europe. Emissions reporting is only as good as the operational data underneath it. That sounds simpler than it is: a ship is not a car. It’s a complex system.”

Building a broad maritime technology group

Tresco equips some 9,000 vessels in European inland shipping with navigation and automation software. Green Maritime opens up a much larger market: thousands of short sea vessels will need emissions monitoring and better operational data in the coming years. Over time, Tresco will bring its inland and seagoing data together on one platform, giving customers a single view of their fleet on inland waterways and at sea.

“Green Maritime gives us a strong position in seagoing shipping, with a product that has proven itself on 220 vessels,” said Bulcke. “The value in maritime technology lies in reliable data on board, a strong market share and deep knowledge of the sector. You don’t copy that with AI. We see room to double the number of connected vessels, and that’s before we look at Southeast Asia.”

Matthias Vandepitte, Managing Partner at Strada Partners and Board Member at Tresco Group: “When we invested in Tresco in 2024, the plan was clear: build on its leadership in inland navigation to create a broad maritime technology group. Green Maritime fits that plan perfectly, with proven technology, a founder who knows the sector from the bridge, and a market that regulation is opening up fast. We’re excited to back Evert and Bart in this next chapter.”

What changes for customers

Green Maritime will remain a separate business unit, led from Apeldoorn by founder and CEO Bart Schut. Seagoing shipping has its own market, language and way of working, so integration will happen step by step. The full team is joining. Existing customers keep their contacts and their service, and gain access to Tresco’s European installation and dealer network and to the group’s R&D capacity.
